findings.title: Worker shutdown can drop queued items or hang
findings.body: The worker checks `self.shutdown` and then blocks in `queue.get()`. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets the flag and calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Work still queued is dropped once the loop exits, and the check at the top of the loop stops draining. Offsets for dropped items are never completed, so they are never committed. A `ShutDown` raised inside `result_processor` is also swallowed by `break`, and the `finally` block then marks the offset complete.

findings.title: queue.ShutDown requires Python 3.13
findings.body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` exist only in Python 3.13+. On older runtimes the `except queue.ShutDown` clause raises AttributeError when an exception is being matched, and `q.shutdown` fails. Worker threads can crash or never stop, and the shutdown path only logs the failure.

findings.title: hash() on str is randomized per process
findings.body: Group-to-queue assignment uses Python's built-in `hash()`, which is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED). After a restart or rebalance, a group can map to a different queue. This is consistent only within one process, but a different consumer process may process the same subscription's messages concurrently. Use a stable hash such as crc32 or md5.

findings.title: Committable offset logic breaks with Kafka offset gaps or after partition revocation
findings.body: The contiguity check requires every integer offset between the start and `max_offset` to be in `all_offsets`. Compacted or transactional topics, or filtered messages that are never submitted, leave gaps, so commits stall permanently. Also, `last_committed` defaults to -1, and tracker state is never cleared on rebalance. A new strategy created with the same shared pool receives stale state.

findings.title: No backpressure; unbounded queues
findings.body: The docstring promises natural backpressure, but the queues are unbounded `queue.Queue()` and `submit` never blocks. A slow worker lets memory and the offset-tracking sets grow without limit.

findings.title: Queue pool is shared across strategies and started in the factory constructor
findings.body: The `FixedQueuePool` is created in `__init__`, with threads started immediately, and shared by every strategy that `create_with_partitions` builds. After a rebalance the old strategy's `close()` calls `queue_pool.shutdown()`. That kills the workers the new strategy relies on, so processing stops. `factory.shutdown` also sets `queue_pool = None`, which breaks later creation.

findings.title: Commit failures and the commit thread
findings.body: `commit_function` is called from a background thread, while arroyo's commit callable is intended for the main consumer thread and is not thread-safe. In addition, `close()` does not run a final commit of completed offsets, so progress is lost on shutdown.
